title: Psalm 90 (Septuagint) = Psalm 91 (KJV)
description: Psalm 90 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 91 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 113. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 113.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 90. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 91. Verse numbers align between the Greek and the KJV in this psalm. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>αινοϲ ωδηϲ τω δαυειδʼ ο κατοικων εν βοηθεια του ϋψιϲτου εν ϲκεπη του θυ του ουρανου αυλιϲθηϲεται <sup>2</sup>ερει τω θω αντιλημπτωρ μου ει και καταφυγη μου ο θϲ μου ελπιω επ αυτον <sup>3</sup>οτι αυτοϲ ρυϲεται με εκ πακιδοϲ θηρευτων και απο λογου ταραχωδουϲ <sup>4</sup>εν τοιϲ μεταφρενοιϲ αυτου επιϲκιαϲει ϲοι και ϋπο ταϲ πτερυγαϲ αυτου ελπιειϲ οπλω κυκλωϲει ϲε η αληθεια αυτου <sup>5</sup>ου φοβηθηϲη απο φοβου νυκτερινου και απο βελουϲ πετομενου ημεραϲ
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. <sup>2</sup>I will say of the LORD,
He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. <sup>3</sup>Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler,
and
 from the noisome pestilence. <sup>4</sup>He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth
shall be thy shield and buckler. <sup>5</sup>Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night;
nor for the arrow
that flieth by day;

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>απο πραγματοϲ διαπορευομενου εν ϲκοτει απο ϲυνπτωματοϲ και δαιμονιου μεϲημβρινου <sup>7</sup>πεϲειται εκ του κλιτουϲ ϲου χιλιαϲ κ(αι) μυριαϲ εκ δεξιων ϲου προϲ ϲε δε ουκ εγγιει <sup>8</sup>πλην τοιϲ οφθαλμοιϲ ϲου κατανοηϲειϲ και ανταποδοϲιν αμαρτωλων οψη <sup>9</sup>οτι ϲυ κε η ελπιϲ μου τον ϋψιϲτον εθου καταφυγην ϲου <sup>10</sup>ου προϲελευϲεται προϲ ϲε κακα και μαϲτιξ ουκ εγγιει τω ϲκηνωματι ϲου
translation.text:
<sup>6</sup>Nor for the pestilence
that walketh in darkness;
nor for the destruction
that wasteth at noonday. <sup>7</sup>A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand;
but it shall not come nigh thee. <sup>8</sup>Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked. <sup>9</sup>Because thou hast made the LORD,
which is my refuge,
even the most High, thy habitation; <sup>10</sup>There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.

translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>οτι τοιϲ αγγελοιϲ αυτου εντελειται περι ϲου του διαφυλαξαι ϲε εν παϲαιϲ ταιϲ οδοιϲ ϲου <sup>12</sup>και επι χειρων αρουϲιν ϲε μηποτε προϲκοψηϲ προϲ λιθον τον ποδα ϲου <sup>13</sup>επ αϲπιδα και βαϲιλιϲκον επιβηϲη και καταπατηϲειϲ λεοντα και δρακοντα <sup>14</sup>οτι επ εμε ηλπιϲεν και ρυϲομαι αυτο ϲκεπαϲω αυτον οτι εγνω το ονομα μου <sup>15</sup>επικαλεϲεται με και ειϲακουϲομαι αυτου μετ αυτου ειμι εν θλιψει και εξελουμαι και δοξαϲω αυτον
translation.text:
<sup>11</sup>For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. <sup>12</sup>They shall bear thee up in
their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone. <sup>13</sup>Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet. <sup>14</sup>Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name. <sup>15</sup>He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I
will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.

translation.original_text: <sup>16</sup>μακροτητι ημερων εμπληϲω αυτον και διξω αυτω το ϲωτηριον μου
translation.text: <sup>16</sup>With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
